problem: The trap says that swapping the indices gives 'an angle above 90°' when n1 > n2. This is not what happens. For n1 > n2 the ratio n1/n2 is greater than 1, and the sine of an angle can never exceed 1, so sin⁻¹(n1/n2) is undefined. There is no angle above 90° at all. A student will take away a wrong idea about the inverse sine.
fix: For the critical angle, use θc = sin⁻¹(n2/n1), not n1/n2. Swapping the indices makes the ratio n1/n2 greater than 1, and sin⁻¹ of a value above 1 does not exist — the formula then wrongly predicts a critical angle where total internal reflection cannot happen.
